_origin: System-attachment ruling. Twelve Start-Up templates target systems, not units; they key the moment their system types exist.
_note: kind='system' rows. BASE-ONLY, and deliberately WITHOUT ATTRIBUTES — a system has no nameplate, and an empty grid is worse than an absent one. The design-basis block is a named deferral, woken by the first real sprinkler acceptance.

mint.name: Sprinkler System
mint.why: The catalog ruled it a system in the equipment audit and refused it as an equipment type. This is that ruling being finished, not reversed.

mint.name: Standpipe System
mint.why: Mint refused as EQUIPMENT on 2026-08-06 for the same reason. Its 11 orphaned items now have a home.

mint.name: Preaction Valve Station
mint.why: A discrete tagged assembly, but system-shaped — it is proven by tripping a system, not by starting a machine.

mint.name: Smoke Management System
mint.why: Decomposes into smoke_control_fan and smoke_control_panel as EQUIPMENT; the system itself is the thing a checklist targets.

mint.name: Egress System
mint.why: Doors, stairs, lighting and their ratings verified as one system.

mint.name: Fire and Smoke Separations
mint.why: A rated-assembly survey across a building — never a unit.

mint.name: Communication System
mint.why: Paging, nurse call and intercom verified as one system.

mint.name: Sprinkler Piping System
mint.why: The piping leg of the sprinkler system, tagged separately in the masters.

mint.name: Hydronic Heating System
mint.why: The Heating System Start-Up Procedure master is a whole-plant sequence, not a boiler.

mint.name: AHU Control System
mint.why: A BAS control sequence. BAS-SPEC owns the module; the TYPE is what a start-up template attaches to.

deferred.detail: Design density, area of operation, hazard classification, water supply and its test date, zone and riser counts, standpipe class.
deferred.why: A system has no nameplate. This block should be designed against a real sprinkler acceptance rather than speculated, and an empty grid is worse than an absent one.
deferred.wakes: The first real project recording a system's design basis — most likely fire protection on a new-construction job.
